Acceptance criteria: the ratified completeness boundary of a unit

|                                      |                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Revision this describes              | `3fdd853314979e03305bc7366b5ac0efdc5bfe14` (`HEAD`) |
| Release presence is reported against | `v3.0.0`                                            |
| Commands on this page                | 12                                                  |
| ...with a stated exit contract       | 6                                                   |

**The register is a declaration, not a behaviour claim.** The command surface is built from `surface/dispatch-table.json`, so the register at a revision states what that revision exposes. It does not state that any of it works. Where this page and your binary disagree, **your binary is right**.

**Exit codes are stated for 6 of these 12 commands, and that is the register's coverage rather than an omission here.** A row carries the exit codes measured on _v2_; whether v3 reproduces them is a separate field. Where the register says v3 corrects v2 without recording what it corrects it to, this page says so instead of reprinting the behaviour the rewrite exists to remove.

**1 description on this page asserts a precondition, flagged inline below.** Refusals have no declared home in the register, so they can only be stated as prose in a help string. The detector that finds them is a regex over English and is therefore a floor, not a ceiling: a precondition phrased without one of its words is invisible to it. Issue `0142`.

## The commands

| Command               | What it does                                                                    | In v3.0.0                        | Reads or writes | Undo       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| `intent ac`           | Acceptance criteria commands                                                    | yes                              | read            | --         |
| `intent ac list`      | List ACs + covering AT + satisfied state                                        | yes                              | read            | --         |
| `intent ac status`    | Report N/M satisfied + verdict (PASS/BLOCKED)                                   | yes                              | read            | --         |
| `intent ac satisfy`   | Satisfy a non-test AC by named evidence                                         | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac unsatisfy` | Reopen a satisfied non-test AC -- clears satisfaction AND its evidence together | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac gate`      | Close-gate: exit non-zero + BLOCKED if unsatisfied                              | yes                              | read            | --         |
| `intent ac descope`   | Record that an AC moved to another thread (non-blocking)                        | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac rescope`   | Undo a descope: back in scope, unsatisfied                                      | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac withdraw`  | Withdraw an AC outright, with its reason on the record (non-blocking)           | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac reinstate` | Undo a withdrawal: back in scope, unsatisfied                                   | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac new`       | Create a criterion (caller-assigned id; refuses an id that is taken)            | yes                              | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent ac edit`      | Reword a criterion, leaving its kind and its satisfaction alone                 | **no -- newer than the release** | mutate          | reversible |

## `intent ac`

Acceptance criteria commands

```
intent ac <command>
```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes                                                        |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | no                                                         |

**Arguments**

| Argument  | Type         | Required | Values | Notes |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `command` | `subcommand` | yes      |        |       |

**v3 corrects v2 here.** Defers to INV-07, now `corrected`: `--help` exits 0 to stdout. The v3 binary already does this.

| Over MCP        | yes        |

| Argument | Type    | Required | Values | Notes |

| `stid`   | `st-id` | yes      |        |       |
| `acid`   | `ac-id` | yes      |        |       |

| Flag         | Takes   | Default | What it does                 |
| ------------ | ------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |

## `intent ac new`

Create a criterion (caller-assigned id; refuses an id that is taken)

**That description asserts a precondition, and nothing checks it.** The register has no structural home for refusals, so a refusal can only be stated as prose in a help string -- which is a contract nothing verifies and nothing updates when the behaviour moves. One of the four such strings in the surface is measured false. See issue `0142`; treat this line as a description, not a guarantee.

```
intent ac new <stid> <acid> [flags]
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | reversible |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type    | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | ------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `stid`   | `st-id` | yes      |        |       |
| `acid`   | `ac-id` | yes      |        |       |

**Flags**

| Flag     | Takes    | Default    | What it does       |
| -------- | -------- | ---------- | ------------------ |
| `--text` | `<text>` |            | The criterion text |
| `--kind` | `<kind>` | `non-test` | Test-backed or not |

**New in v3**, so there is no measured antecedent and the register carries no exit contract for it.

## Refusals

**There is no per-command refusal list, because the register does not carry one.** A row declares its path, arguments, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, MCP exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it refuses. Where a command's exit codes appear above, those _are_ its refusal contract; where they do not, the register has nothing to publish.

The estate-wide roster of refusal variants is in [what Intent ships at this revision](cut-surface.md), taken from a roster that declares itself exhaustive and is checked as one. **It is not attributed to commands anywhere**, and attributing it by reading the variant names would be a guess dressed as a reference.
